senses.gloss:
ज्योता, f., Ved. ‘the brilliant or shining one,’ one
of the mystical names of the cow.

ज्योतिष, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. ज्योतिस्), relating to the
heavenly bodies, astronomical, astrological; (अस्), m.
an astronomer, astrologer; N. of certain magical
formularies for exorcising the evil spirits supposed to
possess weapons; (अम्), n. astronomy, astrology, the
science of the course of the heavenly bodies and divi-
sions of time resting thereon; N. of one of the six
Vedāṅgas or of a short tract which gives only
such a knowledge of the heavenly bodies as was
required for fixing the days and hours of the Vedic
sacrifices; (ई), f. a star, a planet, an asterism.
—ज्यो-
तिष-तत्त्व, अम्, n. or ज्योतिष-रत्नमाला, f., N.
of two works on astronomy.
—ज्योतिष-विद्या, f. astro-
nomical science.
—ज्योतिष-सङ्ग्रह, अस्, m. the
whole science of astronomy.
—ज्योतिषी-मत्, आन्, अती,
अत्, Ved. shining, brilliant; (आन्), m., N. of a par-
ticular sun or form of the sun.
ज्योतिषिक, a wrong form for ज्यौतिषिक, q. v.

ज्योतिष्क, अस्, m. a luminary, a heavenly body;
the luminaries regarded by the Jainas as a class of deities
arranged under five heads, viz. sun, moon, the planets,
fixed stars, and lunar mansions; the plant Premna
Spinosa; the plant Plumbago Zeylanica; the seed of
Trigonella Fœnum Græcum; N. of a Nāga; N. of
a man; (आ), f., N. of a plant, = ज्योतिष्मती; (अम्),
n., N. of a luminous weapon with which Arjuna
destroyed Tamas or darkness personified (see Mahā-
bh. Droṇa-parva 1325); N. of the shining peak of
the Meru.

ज्योतिस्, इस्, n. light in various forms and under various
aspects, as the light of the sun, of dawn, of fire, of
lightning, &c.; brightness or clearness of the sky,
daylight (opposed to Tamas); lightning; light ap-
pearing in three forms, viz. fire on the earth, ether
or air in the intermediate region, and sun in the sky;
a glance of the eye, the faculty of seeing, the eye;
the heavenly bodies, the planets and stars (in this
sense pl., e. g. ज्योतिषाम् अयनम्, the course of the
heavenly bodies); sun and moon (in this sense du.,
e. g. ज्योतिषोर् उपसर्गाः, eclipses &c. of the sun
and moon); the light of heaven, the celestial world;
light as the divine principle of life or as the source
of intelligence, intelligence; light as a type of
freedom, of bliss and of victory, [cf. Lat. lux and Gr.
φάος, φῶς]; N. of the Jyotiṣṭoma as applied to
the first and sixth days of the Abhi-plava ceremony
which lasts six days; N. of certain formularies containing
the word ज्योतिस्; a kind of metre consisting of thirty-
two short and sixteen long syllables; the science of
the course of the heavenly bodies, &c., see ज्योतिष;
a mystical term for the letter र्; (इस्), m. fire; the
[]
sun; N. of the plant Trigonella Fœnum Græcum;
N. of a son of Manu Svārociṣa; also of Marut;
[cf. चित्र-ज्योतिस् and दक्षिणा-ज्˚.]
—ज्योतिः-शास्त्र,
अम्, n. the science of astronomy; a work upon
astronomy.
—ज्योतिः-सामन्, अ, n., N. of a Sāman.
—ज्योतिः-सिद्धान्त, अस्, m. title of an astronomical
work.
—ज्योतिर्-अग्र, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. preceded by
light or life.
—ज्योतिरथ्या, f., N. of a river; (a wrong
form for ज्योती-रथा.)
—ज्योतिर्-अनीक, अस्, आ, अम्,
Ved. having a shining face or appearance.
—ज्योतिर्-
इङ्ग or ज्योतिर्-इङ्गण, अस्, m. ‘moving light,’ a fire-
fly.
—ज्योतिर्-ईश or ज्योतिर्-ईश्वर, अस्, m., N. of the
author of the Dhūrta-samāgama.
—ज्योतिर्-गण, अस्,
m. the heavenly bodies collectively.
—ज्योतिर्-जरायु,
उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. surrounded by a brilliant covering;
(Sāy.) brilliant (among the clouds) like an embryo.
—ज्योतिर्-ज्ञ, अस्, m. ‘star-knower,’ an astrologer,
one versed in astronomy.
—ज्योतिर्-ज्वलनार्चि-श्री-
गर्भ (˚न-अर्˚), अस्, m., N. of a Bodhi-sattva.
—ज्योतिर्-धामन्, आ, m., N. of one of the seven
sages in the Manv-antara of Tāmasa.
—ज्योतिर्-भास-
मणि, इस्, m. a kind of gem.
—ज्योतिर्-भासिन्, ई,
इनी, इ, brilliant with light.
—ज्योतिर्-मण्डल, अम्,
n. the stellar sphere.
—ज्योतिर्-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, con-
sisting of light, brilliant, abounding with stars, starry.
—ज्योतिर्मिलिन्, ई, m. (for -मालिन् ?), a fire-fly.
—ज्योतिर्-मुख, अस्, m., N. of one of the monkey-
followers of Rāma.
—ज्योतिर्-लिङ्ग, अम्, n., N. of
several Liṅga temples.
—ज्योतिर्-लेखावलयिन्, ई,
इनी, इ, studded with rows of stars.
—ज्योतिर्-लोक, अस्,
m. the world of light.
—ज्योतिर्-विद्, त्, त्, त्, knowing
the stars, an astronomer; creating light (in this
sense rt. 3. विद्, to find).
—ज्योतिर्-विद्या, f. the
science of astronomy, astrology.
—ज्योतिर्-वीज, अम्,
n. ‘seed of light,’ a fire-fly.
—ज्योतिर्-हस्ता, f. an
epithet of Durgā.
—ज्योतिश्-चक्र, अम्, n. ‘circle of
the luminaries,’ the zodiac.
—ज्योतिष्-कण, अस्, m.
a spark of fire.
—ज्योतिष्-कर, अस्, m. ‘light-causer,’
a kind of flower.
—ज्योतिष्-कल्प, अस्, आ, अम्, like
flame or fire, blazing, radiant.
—ज्योतिष्कल्प-लता,
f. title of an astrological work.
—ज्योतिष्-कृ, cl. 8.
P. -करोति, -कर्तुम्, to make light, illumine.
—ज्योतिष्-कृत्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. creating light.
—ज्योतिष्-
टम, अस्, आ, अम्, diffusing the most brilliant light.
—ज्योतिष्टोम, अस्, m. (fr. ज्योतिस्-स्तोम), a Soma
ceremony considered as the typical form of a whole
class of ceremonies; it consists of either four or seven
subdivisions, viz. the Agni-ṣṭoma, Ukthya, Ṣoḍa-
śin, Ati-rātra, or in addition to these the Atyagni-
ṣṭoma, Vāja-peya, and Aptor-yāma.
—ज्योतिष्-ट्व,
अम्, n. luminousness, illumination; the condition of
light.
—ज्योतिष्-पक्ष, अस्, आ, अम्, having brilliant
wings.
—ज्योतिष्-प्रभ, अस्, m. ‘brilliant with light,’
N. of a kind of flower; N. of a Buddha; also of a
Bodhi-sattva.
—ज्योतिष्-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, luminous,
brilliant, shining, belonging to the world of light,
heavenly, celestial; ज्योतिष्मती त्रिष्टुप्, a form of
the Triṣṭubh metre, containing three Pādas of twelve
syllables each and one Pāda of eight syllables; (आन्),
m. the sun; N. of one of the seven suns appearing
at the destruction of the world; N. of the third foot
of Brahmā; N. of a son of Manu Svāyambhuva;
also of Manu Sāvarṇa; N. of a king of Kuśa-dvīpa;
also of a son of Priya-vrata; N. of a mountain; (ती),
f. the night (as illumined by the stars), heart-pea,
Cardiospermum Halicacabum.
—ज्योतिस्-सात्, ind. to
flame, to fire or light; ज्योतिस्सात् कृ, to light,
illumine, set on fire.
—ज्योती-रत, अस्, m., N. of a
serpent-demon.
—ज्योती-रथ, अस्, आ, अम्, whose
chariot is light; (Sāy.) bearing fire or the oblation
like a chariot; (अस्), m. the pole-star or in mythology
Dhruva, son of Uttāna-pāda; a kind of serpent;
(आ), f., N. of a river which joins the Śoṇa or Sone.
—ज्योती-रस, अस्, m. a kind of gem.
—ज्योती-रूप-
स्वयम्भू, ऊस्, m. Svayambhū (Brahmā) in the
form of light.
—ज्योती-रूपेश्वर (˚प-ईश्˚), अम्, n.,
N. of a Liṅga.

ज्योत्स्ना, f. a moonlight night; moonlight; light,
splendor in general; N. of one of the bodies of
Brahmā; N. of one of the sixteen Kalās of the
moon; an epithet of Durgā; N. of two plants, =
[]
ज्योत्स्नी and घोषातकी.
—ज्योत्स्ना-काली, f., N. of a
daughter of the moon and wife of Puṣkara who was
a son of Varuṇa.
—ज्योत्स्ना-प्रिय, अस्, m. ‘a friend of
the moonlight,’ the bird Chakora or Greek partridge.
—ज्योत्स्ना-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, illuminated by the moon,
shining, brilliant.
—ज्योत्स्ना-वृक्ष, अस्, m. the
tree or tripod of a lamp, a lamp-stand, candlestick.
—ज्योत्स्नेश (˚ना-ईश), अस्, m. ‘lord or husband of
the moonlight,’ the moon.
ज्योत्स्निका, f., N. of a plant, = कोषातकी.

ज्यो ज्यो, cl. 1. A. ज्यवते, &c., to advise,
instruct, order; observe a vow or any reli-
gious obligation.

ज्योक् ज्योक्, ind. long, for a long time, for
a long while; ज्योक्तमाम्, superl. ind. for the longest
time, longest.
—ज्योग्-जीवातु, उस्, f. long life; ज्योक्
कृ, to be long about anything, delay.

ज्योडि ज्योडि, in names of plants. Cf. कर-
ज्योडि and हस्त-ज्˚.

ज्योतयमानक ज्योतयमानक, अस्, इका, अम्,
Ved. shining (?).

ज्योतिक ज्योतिक, अस्, m., N. of a Nāga;
(perhaps a wrong reading for ज्योतिष्क.)
